messages:
maria: Hey team — opened a docs PR that tries to clarify runtime routing when a requested model isn't available. Holding merge until runtime can confirm the default behavior. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234
jonathan: Quick q — does runtime automatically fallback to another model when the requested one is missing, or is that gated behind a config flag?
maria: Current docs say ‘automatic fallback’ which some reviewers flagged as inaccurate. Need the exact default to avoid shipping wrong guidance.
sophia: runtime: short answer: there are two distinct behaviors and that’s the root cause of confusion.
sophia: (1) allow_model_fallback config — default is false; if set true, the router will try cross-family fallbacks per policy.
sophia: (2) variant routing — an internal optimization that may route to compatible variants within the same pinned model family even when allow_model_fallback is false.
maria: Ugh — that split is exactly what's causing the docs mismatch. Can you give one clear sentence we can paste into the PR?
sophia: Suggestion to paste: "Default behavior: allow_model_fallback is false. The system may perform variant routing within the same model family (compatible tokenizer/architecture); explicit cross-family fallback only occurs if allow_model_fallback is set to true in the route config."
johnathan: small nit: variant routing has an additional token-length heuristic — it only considers variants for short sequences (<512 tokens) to avoid cold-start KV cache blowups. Should we call that out?
sophia: Good catch. Add one more short clause: "Variant routing is limited by sequence-length and compatibility checks (typically applied for sequences <512 tokens)."
maria: I'll add both sentences. Also the PR's SDK example shows JSON with allow_model_fallback omitted (implying default true). I'll change that to explicitly set false and add a note.
deploy-bot: Preview deployed for PR 1234: https://docs-preview.internal/pr/1234 — linkcheck: 1 warning (external link flagged).
johnathan: Another edge: Dedicated clusters may be configured by account policy to enable managed fallback even if route config omits allow_model_fallback. Worth a short parenthetical for enterprise customers.
sophia: That's correct — account-level policy can override. We'll say "Account policies can enable managed fallback on Dedicated deployments."
maria: OK — new wording pushed. Anyone object to merging after I update the examples?
johnathan: LGTM after the explicit example change.
sophia: LGTM.
maria: Merging in ~10m unless someone raises a last-minute point. :thumbsup:
